summary: Master Political Economy Analysis for Development Programming to improve feasibility, adapt programmes, and write sharper PEA briefings. Enrol now.
lede: Political economy analysis for development programming helps professionals assess how power, institutions, interests and incentives shape programme feasibility and results. It is for programme managers, policy analysts, MEL specialists and governance advisers who need to map stakeholders, diagnose formal and informal constraints, and identify possible change pathways. Learners practise applying these findings to programme design, sequencing, risk responses and decision-focused reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to read the political environment around development programming and turn that analysis into better design, sequencing, and reporting.
prerequisites: You should bring familiarity with at least one development programme, policy process, or governance intervention. Prior exposure to Theory of Change thinking, stakeholder analysis, or monitoring and evaluation will help you move faster through the applied exercises, but it is not mandatory.
